body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)=\{A_{vu}z/(1-A_{vv}z):(A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\}\), with \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,m,G}(B,Q)\) returning its unique element or two attained unequal elements

sampling_model.design: The main identifying and certification class is a single stationary Gaussian fine-grid VAR(1), observed at times \(0,m,\ldots,nm\), with known \(m\), supplied labeled process DAG \(G\), triangular transition, and diagonal fine innovation covariance. The even-factor sign corollary is deliberately broader: it permits an arbitrary stable transition and arbitrary positive-definite Gaussian innovation covariance and needs no supplied order.
sampling_model.units: The sampling units are the \(n+1\) dependent coarse-time vectors \((Y_0,\ldots,Y_n)\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no binary treatment; the causal query is the direct fine-grid transfer along the supplied process edge \(u\to v\).
sampling_model.overlap: There is no treatment-overlap condition. The stability margin gives \(|1-A_{vv}z|\ge\gamma>0\) on \(\mathbb T\), which is the support condition needed for the rational transfer.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(M_0,M_1\) by overlapping empirical lag moments and form \(\widehat B=\widehat M_1\widehat M_0^{-1}\). On the odd regular class, compute the exact finite \(m\)-step algebraic dependency closure seeded at \(u\to v\), recover only its incident diagonals and retained edges, propagate the Isserlis long-run covariance through that Jacobian, and report simultaneous Wald disks. The directed-path corridor and global derivative-separated estimators agree on the target and give simpler sufficient corollaries. Outside the exact-local regular class, invert the rationally outward-rounded moment box through all compatible fine-grid branches without selecting one.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Gong et al. obtain positive fine-model recovery under non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions, and separately note generic nonuniqueness under Gaussian data.
We present a unifying framework for parameter identifiability and estimation under both subsampling and mixed frequencies when the shocks are non-Gaussian.
The algorithm forms a Schur decomposition and computes a \(p\)-th root of the triangular factor by a recursion.
The spectral latent-factor half-trek criterion identifies direct link functions by rational operations on the spectral density.
We characterise the asymptotic distribution of causal effect and spectral contribution estimators in terms of algebraic relations dictated by the process graph.
We establish useful deviation bounds for dependent Gaussian data using a spectral measure of stability.
We prove an exponential probability tail inequality for positive semidefinite quadratic forms in a subgaussian random vector.
The results about coverage probability are stated in a nonasymptotic way and apply for small and moderate sample size.
We provide a constraint satisfaction procedure for system-timescale causal structures corresponding to a measurement-timescale structure.
Classical CAD projection algorithms preserve chordal structure when projection follows a perfect elimination ordering.
In the regular mixed-frequency VARMA case with moving-average order exceeding autoregressive order, generic local identification fails.

body.tldr: Subsampling turns a fine-grid process DAG into a matrix-root problem, so a queried causal transfer is governed by the compatible fiber rather than by a selected numerical root. For odd \(m\), seed the queried edge and close only under graph-supported monomial variables that occur in its finite \(m\)-step remainders: noncollision and root-derivative separation on this exact terminating dependency set identify the transfer and yield simultaneous Wald disks. The directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) path corridor is a readable sufficient superset and its earlier identification and Wald results remain corollaries. For even \(m\), the same-law sign obstruction continues to hold on the larger unrestricted stable Gaussian VAR(1) class with arbitrary positive-definite innovations. Exact transfer-aware certification and branch-free confidence-region inversion cover singular and nonregular cases.

project_justification.gap: Published subsampling results either use non-Gaussian shocks for positive recovery, enumerate qualitative graph equivalence classes, or choose a numerical matrix-root branch. Gong et al.'s positive theorem assumes non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions, so neither it nor the present Gaussian supplied-order result contains the other. Prior root recursions also do not isolate, for one causal transfer, the exact finite set of graph-supported monomial dependencies induced by the known sampling factor.
project_justification.niche: A supplied causal order makes triangular divided-difference recursion available. For the direct transfer, the sharp recursive locality is obtained by seeding \(u\to v\) and repeatedly adding only allowed off-diagonal variables that actually occur in retained \(m\)-step remainder monomials, together with their incident diagonals. This exact closure terminates, is contained in the directed path corridor, and can be strictly smaller; the path corridor remains an interpretable sufficient graphical screen.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an explicit exact-dependency identifying map and simultaneous Wald disks on a nonempty compact class separated only on that finite set, while retaining the path-corridor and globally separated theorems as successive corollaries. It also gives an unrestricted stable-Gaussian even-sign obstruction with arbitrary positive-definite innovations, plus a total transfer-aware CAD fallback with attained witnesses and finite-sample branch-free inversion. The covariance-envelope fallback remains a validity device equal pathwise to the deterministic box, not a claimed adaptive improvement.

body.related_work: Gong et al. (2015) motivate temporal causal recovery from subsampled data. Their positive recovery theorem uses non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions; the present positive result instead uses Gaussian innovations, a supplied order, and process-DAG restrictions, so the two positive classes are incomparable rather than related by inclusion. Their Gaussian nonuniqueness discussion motivates the obstruction, while the present proof isolates an even-factor sign pair on the strictly larger stable Gaussian VAR(1) class with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance and no order or triangularity requirement. Tank, Fox, and Shojaie (2019) likewise use non-Gaussian shocks and likelihood methods. Hyttinen et al. (2017) preserve qualitative subsampling ambiguity through exact constraints, whereas the present target is a numerical rational transfer. Smith (2003), Bini, Higham, and Meini (2005), and Higham (2008) supply triangular-root algorithms and branch theory; the new step derives the exact finite \(m\)-step graph-supported monomial dependency closure for one queried transfer, proves its terminating recursion, and retains the larger directed-path corridor as a readable corollary before combining graph zeros, innovation covariance, transfer equality, and complete-fiber certification. Reiter et al. (2026) identify rational link effects from an unaliased fine-grid spectrum, and Reiter et al. (2024) derive local delta-method inference once fine-grid coefficients are differentiably estimable. Basu and Michailidis (2015), Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang (2012), and Giurcanu and Spokoiny (2004) provide concentration context for finite-sample moment regions. Mixed-frequency VARMA and unit-root results of Deistler, Koelbl, and Anderson (2017), Anderson et al. (2016), and Gersing, Sögner, and Deistler (2023) concern different model classes.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact-dependency result still assumes a supplied scientifically defensible order and a known odd sampling factor for positive identification; it does not infer the order. The closure is exact for formal graph-supported monomial dependence in the stated triangular recursion, not a claim that every retained coefficient is numerically influential at every parameter value. Genericity is in fine-parameter space, not observed-law image space. Exact CAD certifies termination but not polynomial-time scalability, and executable witnesses require effective real-closed-field input. Gong et al.'s Temperature--Ozone example is used only as a conditional \(m=2\) Gaussian ambiguity audit if external science supplies the one-way order; their fit does not establish that order, and their positive non-Gaussian theorem is not imported into this Gaussian class.
body.honest_scope: Positive identification and Wald inference concern stable, ordered, finite-dimensional Gaussian VAR(1) process-DAG models with known odd subsampling factor and diagonal fine innovation covariance. Point identification and smooth recovery of \(h_{uv}\) require noncollision and derivative separation only on the exact finite \(m\)-step algebraic dependency closure seeded at \(u\to v\). This closure is contained in, and can be strictly smaller than, the directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) path corridor; the corridor and global separation results remain nonempty sufficient corollaries. Coefficients and innovation variances outside the relevant set may remain ambiguous, and no full-matrix uniqueness is claimed. In contrast, the even-factor sign obstruction holds for every stable Gaussian VAR(1) with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance, even without a supplied order, triangularity, or graph zeros, whenever the queried coordinate is nonzero. Outside the exact-local regular class, inference is branch-free. No claim is made about unknown sampling factors, high-dimensional rates, VARMA or unit-root extensions, or the scientific validity of the Temperature--Ozone ordering.
